    Belmont Cameli Has Arrived: VMAN 57 Crowns Hollywood’s New Leading Man

    Share
    Facebook
    X
    Pinterest
    WhatsApp
      Listen to audio version of this article
      Sponsored by
      0:00 / 6:39
      Instaread
      fashionablymale
      August 31, 2026

      There are moments when Hollywood seems to collectively decide that an actor’s time has arrived. For Belmont Cameli, that moment appears to be happening right now.

      The Off Campus star commands attention in VMAN 57, photographed by the legendary duo Luigi & Iango in a striking portrait of contemporary masculine beauty. Bare skin, Cartier jewelry, Burberry trousers and an impressive athletic physique turn Cameli into something increasingly rare in modern celebrity culture: a convincing new Hollywood leading man.

      And perhaps the timing couldn’t be better.

      The Making of a Leading Man

      VMAN approaches Cameli’s rise from an interesting perspective: turning 30—or getting close to it—is hardly late for an actor to have his breakthrough.

      Quite the opposite.

      The magazine places Cameli within a remarkable Hollywood tradition, looking back at actors including Montgomery Clift, Marlon Brando, Robert De Niro, Harrison Ford, Sylvester Stallone, Denzel Washington, Brad Pitt and Austin Butler, whose careers reached transformative moments around their late twenties or early thirties.

      It makes Cameli’s ascent feel less like an overnight sensation and more like the result of preparation finally meeting opportunity.

      After nearly a decade working as an actor, his role as hockey player Garrett Graham in Off Campus has introduced him to a considerably larger audience. Cameli had already appeared in projects including the Saved by the Bell revival, but Off Campus pushed him into another level of visibility.

      Suddenly there are edits, fancams, TikToks and an audience paying very close attention.

      But VMAN’s photographs suggest something beyond the popularity of a television character.

      They present the actor as a star.

      Luigi & Iango Understand the Assignment

      And this is where the Fashionably Male eye naturally takes over.

      See also  FIGHT PLAN BY KARL SIMONE

      Luigi & Iango know exactly how to photograph a man.

      There is an almost classical simplicity to the images. Instead of burying Cameli underneath elaborate fashion, the photographers allow his face and physique to dominate the frame.

      His athletic proportions become part of the styling itself.

      Broad shoulders, a developed chest and a naturally masculine frame provide a powerful background for pieces from Cartier’s Juste un Clou collection, including necklaces, rings, bracelets and an ear jewel. A Cartier Roadster watch adds another layer of polished masculinity, while Burberry trousers complete the pared-back wardrobe in several photographs.

      The contrast works beautifully.

      Precious jewelry against bare skin could easily become overly decorative. Here, it does the opposite. The gold and white-gold pieces trace Cameli’s physique, catching the light while emphasizing the neck, wrists, hands and torso.

      Luxury becomes sensual.

      And masculinity doesn’t disappear underneath the jewelry—it becomes even more pronounced.

      The Male Body as Luxury

      There is also something refreshingly direct about seeing a male celebrity photographed this way.

      Cameli isn’t hiding behind a character, oversized tailoring or an elaborate set. Luigi & Iango reduce the visual language to its essentials: man, body, jewelry, light and camera.

      The result recalls an older tradition of Hollywood portraiture when the camera helped construct the mythology surrounding a leading man.

      Except this is unmistakably 2026.

      Men’s relationship with jewelry has expanded dramatically, and Cartier’s presence throughout the editorial feels completely natural. Necklaces, bracelets, rings, watches and even an ear jewel become part of Cameli’s masculine vocabulary rather than accessories fighting against it.

      It is also impossible to ignore his physicality.

      Cameli possesses the kind of physique that photographs extraordinarily well: athletic rather than exaggerated, strong without becoming bodybuilder-heavy, and proportional enough that clothing and jewelry complement rather than compete with his body.

      See also  Andrej Pejic by Kristiina Wilson

      There is discipline visible there.

      For a character like Garrett Graham—and for an actor entering the modern leading-man conversation—that physical presence matters.

      Belmont Cameli Is Suddenly Everywhere

      Yet perhaps the most interesting thing about his current moment is Cameli’s attitude toward it.

      In a separate VMAN 57 conversation with Grammy-winning musician Laufey, the actor admits that the sudden attention has required some adjustment.

      He explains that fame itself was never the objective. Success as an actor was.

      Cameli talks about discovering that something as ordinary as walking around New York for the day has become more complicated now that people recognize him. Still, his hope is refreshingly practical: that all this attention creates opportunities to do more—and better—work.

      He also deliberately keeps some distance from internet commentary, recognizing the danger in allowing praise or criticism from strangers to determine how he feels about himself.

      That’s a particularly useful instinct for someone experiencing the intensity of a modern breakout.

      Because today’s Hollywood star isn’t simply watched on a screen.

      He’s clipped, edited, reposted, GIFed, thirsted over and pushed through millions of algorithmically generated feeds.

      Cameli has entered exactly that machine.

      More Than the Handsome Guy

      There is another reason his trajectory becomes interesting.

      He clearly doesn’t intend to stop at being the handsome actor currently occupying everyone’s feed.

      Cameli tells Laufey that he wants to direct and write, with comedy being particularly important to him. He grew up admiring performers including Robin Williams and comedy figures such as David Letterman and Norm Macdonald.

      He has even considered developing a drama centered around ballet, inspired partly by his sister’s experience as a ballerina and his fascination with the discipline and athleticism behind the art form.

      See also  Sergio Acevedo by HardCiderNY

      That ambition makes this VMAN moment feel less like a destination and more like an introduction.

      Perfect Timing, Indeed

      Hollywood has always loved the discovery of its next leading man.

      Every generation gets its moment when an actor seems to emerge at precisely the right intersection of talent, physical presence, charisma and opportunity.

      Belmont Cameli may be standing at that intersection now.

      VMAN makes the historical argument by looking toward the actors who found defining opportunities around the same age.

      Luigi & Iango make the visual argument.

      Their camera presents Cameli with remarkably little distraction. There is confidence in that decision. When you have a subject capable of carrying the photograph, you don’t need much else.

      A masculine physique.

      Exceptional jewelry.

      A pair of trousers.

      A face Hollywood is quickly learning to recognize.

      Sometimes that’s enough.

      Belmont Cameli has arrived. Now comes the interesting part: seeing what he does with the moment.
